big_story.headline: Jio Targets Record Listing
big_story.subhead: RELIANCE DIGITAL ARM SETS IPO PRICE BAND TO RAISE UP TO ₹30,200 CRORE
paragraphs: Jio Platforms is preparing for India's biggest initial public offering with a targeted valuation of ₹10.3 lakh crore. The digital arm of Reliance Industries has reportedly set its price band between ₹1,065 and ₹1,119 per share. The company aims to raise up to ₹30,200 crore through this market debut. Sources indicate that this listing could value the telecom giant at approximately $106 billion.

The mega listing comes as conglomerate Reliance Industries looks to unlock value from its digital and telecom operations. Investors have closely watched the price band disclosure following weeks of market speculation. By fixing the upper band at ₹1,119, the firm establishes a clear benchmark for public investors. This issue is set to become one of the most prominent capital market events in domestic corporate history.

Market participants are evaluating how this massive liquidity requirement will impact broader equity flows. The listing will provide fresh domestic scale while testing retail and institutional appetite. Market watchers will closely observe allotment details and subscription metrics as the issue proceeds toward completion. The capital raised will mark a major structural milestone for the digital giant.
big_story.pullbox: Jio Platforms aims to raise ₹30,200 crore at a valuation of ₹10.3 lakh crore, setting a new benchmark for Indian market listings.

explains.title: What is an IPO Price Band?
paragraphs: An IPO price band is the minimum and maximum price range within which investors can bid for shares in an initial public offering. The lower figure is known as the floor price, while the higher figure is the cap price.

During the subscription window, institutional and retail bidders submit orders specifying the quantity and price within this range. Once bidding closes, the issuing firm calculates the final offer price based on overall market demand.

Wealth management startup Zomint has successfully raised ₹36 crore in its latest funding round. The investment was led by prominent venture capital firms Lightspeed and Prime Venture Partners. The startup provides technology-driven wealth management services to growing investor segments.

The fresh capital injection will help the company expand its service offerings and technological capabilities. Backing from established venture capital investors highlights ongoing interest in digital financial services across India. The funding round positions Zomint to scale its wealth tech operations.

story_1.headline: India Selected to Host WTTC Global Summit 2027
paragraphs: India has officially been selected to host the prestigious WTTC Global Summit 2027. Recognized widely as the world's most important tourism event, the gathering brings together global industry leaders and policymakers.

The announcement highlights the nation's growing prominence on the international tourism stage. Preparations for the landmark event are already drawing significant attention from hospitality and travel sectors.

geopolitics.headline: India-US Trade Deal Faces Policy Friction
paragraphs: Economic tensions between India and the US are becoming more visible amid tougher US immigration policies and trade uncertainty. Following Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's plateau remark, officials clarified that the trade agreement is done and only fine print remains. However, political dynamics surrounding the 2026 US midterms indicate a Democratic House may not necessarily ease tariff pressure on Indian goods.

Strategic friction is growing as observers note the US wants India's power without accommodating its strategic autonomy. In response to persistent trade uncertainty, India's pharma industry is officially looking beyond the USA for growth. Businesses must now recalibrate supply chains to navigate shifting tariffs, immigration restrictions, and evolving trade terms.
